newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks pare losses at close.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks pare losses at close.

text.p: Argentine stocks recouped some losses to close moderately lower Tuesday in a market troubled by former Economy Minister Domingo Cavallo's accusations of government corruption, dealers said.

"Cavallo's allegations caused some concern and created a volatile tone," said Gabriel Armando of brokers Galicia Valores. "But the market clearly had to perform a correction, and this political turbulence has simply helped speed up the process."
The bolsa's blue-chip MerVal index .MERV shed 0.9 percent to 578.85, pulling off a session low of 573.73.
Cavallo, who first denounced "mafias" in Peronist circles more than one year ago, Tuesday stepped up his crusade against government corruption.
Speaking to Argentine radio from New York, he accused Interior Minister Carlos Corach and Justice Minister Elias Jassan of manipulating judges and trying to cover up different corruption probes.

"When the markets learned of Cavallo's statements they took a pretty big hit, especially the telephone stocks which are generally trend-setters. But then they recovered a lot," said Juan Pablo Paillot at traders Ravello.
Talk of graft has spread ever since the courts cracked a $3.0 billion smuggling ring in customs earlier this month and President Carlos Menem launched a special investigation.
Traders said the bolsa would stay tuned to the corruption debate Wednesday but might have already found a floor.
"Stocks remain somewhat overbought, and there may be some more selective selling, but today's partial bounceback with better volume could mean the market has already bottomed out," said Armando.
The broad market shed 0.7 percent, with losers beating winners 34 to 11 and 18 issues closing flat.
Floor volume swelled to 15.6 million pesos from a dismal 7.4 million traded Monday during the U.S. Columbus Day holiday, while over-the-counter deals totalled 114.5 million.
Heaviest main-tier losers were carmaker Sevel, textile firm and shoemaker Alpargatas and power utility Central Puerto, which fell 3.4 percent, 2.4 percent and 2.2 percent, respectively.
The only gainers were Banco Frances, which jumped 2.3 percent, real estate developer Irsa, up 0.9 percent, and oil firms Astra and YPF, up 0.6 percent and 0.2 percent each.
